analysis:
I examined the TB-012/T-059/A-018 add-on hold surface and found no regression.

AddonIPCServer.swift (head):
- The peer audit token is now verified before a connection takes one of the 8 slots (line 138). Unauthenticated same-UID peers are refused at once with a small response and close.
- A new 10s requestTimeout (lines 32, 178-185) bounds trickled partial lines. It sits beside the 300s idle timeout and the maximumMessageBytes cap.
- Per-request re-verification remains (line 207).
- Together these close a slot-exhaustion path that let an unsigned local process keep the add-on out. That is hardening for T-059.
- Residual: authenticate() now runs on the single accept thread. A slow code-signing check, or a flood of refused peers, would serialize accepts. Each refused peer also logs a warning (line 219), so a flood means log spam. This is only a local same-UID availability concern. The AddonPeerPolicy cost is not in this batch.

ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:
- cancelAllInflight is replaced at drain timeout by cancelRequestsOutlivingAddonHoldDrain (head lines 282-292).
  - It snapshots inflightTasks plus requestToModel keys, excluding engineV2 recovery pins.
  - It rechecks hold ownership before each cancellation, so work accepted after a release is not killed.
  - It cancels via handleCancellation(receivedFromCoordinator:false). That handler is not shown here. Integration should confirm it still sends the fail-closed terminal error to the coordinator (T-010, and T-008 for no plaintext) and releases engine/KV state.
- unloadAllModelsForAddonHold now waits, unbounded, for isLoadingAny to clear (lines 311-317). A hung load keeps the hold in draining; admission stays closed, so the effect is availability-only.
- addonHoldSettleTimeout became an instance property (line 300). Its definition is not visible; confirm it is not configurable externally in production.

Load fence:
- addonHoldLoadRefusal (lines 340-343) is applied only in the NativeMiMo load recheck (ProviderLoop+NativeMiMo.swift head line 251).
- Integration should verify that other model-load and slot-publish paths (EngineV2, preload, desired_models) consult the same fence. If they do not, models could load beside the VMs, which is the stated T-059 risk. The visible code does not establish a gap.

Nothing here touches encryption, attestation, or App Attest authorization. The hold still never stops the App Attest worker.
